entries.conditions: Whole-graph compile of a ~930 MB fp16 flatbuffer. A 930 MB fp16 vision graph compiles whole (3104/3104 nodes, 1 partition) and runs at 9.2 s per image on a Pixel 8a; first-launch shader compilation costs about 50 s. Resident set for the compiled graph is roughly 2.5x the flatbuffer size, which is what bounds how many such graphs can be live at once.

evidence.source_model: SAM 3.1 vision trunk (ViT-L/14 @1008)

entries.conditions: A DETR-style decoder head that 2.1.5 mis-executes runs correctly on 2.2.0: the same .tflite, same device, same app, only the runtime version differing. On 2.1.5 all 200 query logits come back identical (std 0.0) while boxes and masks are fine; on 2.2.0 the kept set matches PyTorch (scores within 0.02, mask IoU 0.981-0.996).

evidence.source_model: SAM 3.1 detection head (200-query DETR decoder)

rewrite_hints.expected_effect: decoder logits match the desktop reference
rewrite_hints.rewrite: pin the runtime to 2.2.0 for this graph shape; the rank-4 authoring alone is not sufficient on 2.1.5
rewrite_hints.symptom: identical logits across every query on 2.1.5; correct on 2.2.0

entries.conditions: XNNPACK CPU delegation of a 607 MB CLIP-L text encoder is complete on 2.2.0 (1627/1627 nodes, 0.5 s) where 2.1.5 delegates 1337/1627 and takes 1.9 s on the same device and file.

evidence.source_model: SAM 3.1 text encoder

rewrite_hints.symptom: partial CPU delegation and ~4x slower execution on 2.1.5

entries.conditions: Constant LHS (baked interpolation matrix) x runtime RHS refuses whole-graph compile. Runtime-activation x runtime-activation BMMs delegate normally (attention probes). Constraint added 2026-09-25 (owner: 推奨で): operand_a=constant — the constant-LHS case; runtime x runtime BMMs are the separate delegated row.

evidence.source_model: probe_rbmm (npubench/factors phase8.log m_rbmm_gpu)

rewrite_hints.expected_effect: compiles; also 1.41x faster on the NPU (perf_factors bilinear-constmatmul-to-builtin-resize)
rewrite_hints.rewrite: use builtin RESIZE_BILINEAR (align_corners=true now supported) instead of the const-matmul lowering
rewrite_hints.symptom: const-matmul bilinear form fails GPU compile

entries.conditions: Weight-only int8 DEQUANTIZE feeding FULLY_CONNECTED refuses whole-graph compile on the S26 Adreno (LiteRtException: Failed to compile model). The same graph with fp32 weights or fp16+DEQUANTIZE compiles and runs (4.58 ms). Upstream answer on the same graph form, weight-only int8 through an explicit DEQUANTIZE into FULLY_CONNECTED (LiteRT #9523: `Shape mismatch: {bhwc, {576, 1, 1, 576}} vs {bhwc, {1, 1, 576, 576}}` on Metal, Android OpenCL and macOS WebGPU; 2026-10-01T03:50:36Z, https://github.com/google-ai-edge/LiteRT/issues/9523#issuecomment-5924360785): the mismatch "is caused by inconsistent 2D-to-4D `BHWC` auto-expansion conventions across the dequantize and FC paths. Currently, aligning shapes explicitly via `RESHAPE` prior to delegate ingestion is the only workaround". This entry's log has no error text beyond `Failed to compile model`, so the link is by graph form only. Closed as a duplicate of the tracking issue LiteRT #10445 (opened 2026-10-01: standard shape broadcasting, or automatic 4D RESHAPE insertion for lower- and mixed-rank inputs, in the MLDrift GPU delegate).

evidence.source_model: gemv probe: 8x Linear(4096x4096)+ReLU T=1 chain (npubench/factors phase9.log m_gemv_int8_gpu vs m_gemv_fp32_gpu)

rewrite_hints.expected_effect: compiles and runs; weight-only quantization buys no latency on either accelerator anyway (perf_factors gemv-weight-dtype-bandwidth-null)
rewrite_hints.rewrite: store weights fp32 or fp16+DEQUANTIZE for the GPU lane
rewrite_hints.symptom: whole-graph GPU compile fails on a DRQ-int8 weight file
